A1.justification: Both readable, complete 12-page PDFs describe the same GtR research. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original ImageNet and GenEval experiments, including quantitative comparisons, GtR/FTS ablations and generated examples in Tables 1–5 and Figures 5–6.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original ImageNet and GenEval experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations and generated examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical hierarchical stage partitioning, intra-stage generation, stage-aware diffusion scheduling and Frequency-Weighted Token Selection. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet class-conditional generation at 256×256 and LightGen text-to-image generation on GenEval at 512×512. No datasets, tasks or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical comparator membership, including reduced-step, Halton, DiSA and LazyMAR comparisons for MAR, and the same LightGen and other text-to-image baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same model configurations, resolutions, sampling schedules and metrics. ImageNet evaluation still uses 50,000 images across 1,000 classes, with FID, IS, FLOPs and latency measurements.

E4.justification: Tables 3–5 retain identical component, token-selection and sampling-order ablations. The diagnostic comparisons in Figures 1–3 and qualitative examples in Figures 5–6 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. Figure 3 retains the same qualitative comparison using different random seeds.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports MAR-H + GtR at FID 1.59, IS 304.4 and 3.72× speedup in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), token-partition definitions, probability factorizations and Fourier-based importance scoring are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about training-free GtR acceleration, FTS and comparable generation quality, including the 3.72× MAR-H speedup claim.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning spatial token dependencies, early semantic structure, easier reconstruction and high-frequency token complexity are unchanged, as are the sampling-order interpretations in Section 4.4.

D1.justification: Implementation details, tokenizers, stage counts, generation rates and diffusion-step settings in Section 4.1 are identical. Both versions retain the same code-release statement and repository link.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper and the complete reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to autoregressive and masked generation methods remains identical.

P1.justification: The first-page affiliation list swaps Beijing Institute of Technology and EPIC Lab, SJTU between labels 1 and 2, with corresponding author superscripts updated. Author–institution associations remain the same. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; body wording and structure do not.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–5 and Algorithm 1 retain identical formatting, captions and placement. Pages 2–12 render identically; first-page differences are confined to affiliation and version text within the existing layout.

improvement.justification: The revision only reorders and renumbers affiliations and updates the arXiv stamp. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations and reproducibility information are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
